literal: Those who perform penance without eating are great; (but they are) behind those who endure the harsh words spoken by others.
translation: Those who perform penance by fasting are indeed great, but they stand only behind those who patiently endure the harsh words spoken by others.
modern: உணவு உண்ணாமல் நோன்பு நோற்பவர்கள் பெருமை உடையவர்கள் ஆவர்; ஆனால், அவர்கள் பிறர் பேசும் கொடுமையான சொற்களைப் பொறுத்துக் கொள்பவர்களுக்குப் பின்னேதான் நிற்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares physical fasting with emotional forbearance. While fasting (abstaining from food) is traditionally considered a high spiritual achievement, the poet argues that enduring the bitter, hurtful words of others requires a far greater strength of character. Therefore, those who practice patience and forgiveness are placed on a higher pedestal than those who merely subject their bodies to physical austerities. The key word 'நோல்' (to endure or perform penance) is used in both contexts to show that bearing insults is itself the ultimate form of penance.
